content.thinking:
I'm piecing together the postmortem's causal chain: account pages failed for many shoppers, citing the error rate metrics, then tracing it back to requests raising a ZeroDivisionError at some point in the code.

I'm then tracing that this code path ran because the monthly-spend feature flag was switched on, and I'm ruling out other candidates — an unrelated feature flag toggled after onset, no deploys around the incident window, and baseline pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors that predate the onset and aren't related.

The mitigation confirms this: reverting the flag and restoring the service fixed things. For the final why, the function divides by the count of purchases this month, which is empty for shoppers with past purchases but none this month — and this code only runs when the flag is true, so this is a genuine root cause resting on an unrun reading rather than a known fix.

I should trace timing precisely: the flag was flipped at P1, read by G971b at 15:23, and T15 pulled the flag's provider history. I can rule out the unrelated feature toggle in P2 since it switched on after the onset, so it couldn't be the cause, and I can rule out a deploy since no new revisions appeared — rollout had already converged on one revision per T9 and T10.

Looking at the contributing factors now, it seems the flag change hit all traffic nearly at once rather than through a gradual rollout — G971b shows most evaluations flipped within about a minute. That points toward a missing staged rollout with automated error-rate checks as a key gap, and I'm also noting the absence of any test coverage for this.

For the second factor, there's a missing test that would've caught accounts with past purchases but no activity this month on the monthly-summary path — that's a distinct gap from the mitigation itself, so I should propose requiring tests for flag-gated paths before enabling a flag in CI.

For the third factor, I'm weighing whether paging an on-call engineer would have actually changed the outcome, since Argus's automated mitigation resolved things quickly on its own — it's not clear a human response would have shortened the incident.

That nobody was paged still feels like a finding worth noting on its own, so I'll log it under went_wrong and separately propose linking the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging as an action item, even without a clear counterfactual answer.

Now I'm moving to compiling what went well, starting with the investigator correctly forming the alert-raised event and the mitigation agent's revert action.

The timeline continues to shape up well: Argus confirmed the flag revert fixed things shortly after the alert, Code-Fix got a draft PR up quickly, and Argus caught the P2 issue by digging through flag history even outside the main investigation window. I'm also noting some luck involved — the failures happened to be limited to shoppers with past purchases but nothing this month, and the fact that the flag was cleanly reversible made mitigation simpler than it could have been.

What went wrong mainly comes down to nobody paging on this. For what's still at risk, I'm flagging that the division logic in the monthly summary code is untouched, so re-enabling monthly-spend-feature would likely cause the same account page failures for shoppers with past-but-not-recent purchases — the fix didn't address that underlying issue, just worked around it.

For action items, I'm proposing a gradual rollout of flag changes on io-shop starting with a small traffic share and auto-halt on error spikes, a CI check that exercises io-shop's tests with each feature flag enabled so untested flag-gated paths can't ship, and linking the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so this doesn't go unnoticed again.

Leaving CF-1 and CF-2's addressed_by fields empty since AI-2's tests cover the check gap but don't directly answer the fault. For the root cause, I'm pinning it down precisely: render_spend_summary only runs when use_monthly_summary is enabled, and it computes average spend by dividing the month's total by the count of purchases marked this month — for a returning shopper with no purchases this month, that count is zero, triggering a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py line 47 and crashing the account page request.

I should note this assumption rests on Code-Fix's interpretation rather than the logs directly showing which shoppers failed. For the symptom, I can cite the error rate spike using Gbac1 and G5309 without needing specific metric labels. For CF-1, I have evidence from G971b and Gce95 showing the flag rollout wasn't staged — nearly all evaluations flipped to "on" within the first minute, with no gradual ramp.

I'll avoid citing evidence labels directly in the prose narrative, keeping them as backing references instead. Now I'll pull in the durations for the went_well section and finish writing everything up.

action_items.item: Roll out feature-flag changes on io-shop gradually, starting with a small share of traffic, and halt the rollout automatically when the error rate rises.

Add a CI check that runs io-shop's tests with each feature flag switched on, including accounts with past purchases but none this month, and require it to pass before a flag can be enabled in production.
Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests failed for many shoppers. Across all of the service's requests, the share that failed rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The service's own account-page error-rate log line peaked at {Gbac1.5}.

The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That error appears in the logs from the onset minute onward and in none of the lines read before it.

ruled_out.what: The feature flag an-unrelated-feature, switched on at {P2.1}. That came after the onset at {began}, when the division errors had already started.
A deploy. The read of production changes returned no deploy, only the flag change. As of {T10.1}, all replicas ran one revision.

causal_chain.step: That code ran because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}. Before then every evaluation of the flag returned off and account pages rendered normally. In the onset minute most evaluations returned on, and every evaluation after that minute did. Turning the flag off at {T18.1} brought the service back to normal, and the action was judged confirmed at {T21.1}. According to Code-Fix's reading, `render_spend_summary` calls the failing function only when `use_monthly_summary` is true.

The failing function, `average_spend_per_item_this_month`, divides the month's total by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError on every page view by such a shopper.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on account pages started a calculation that failed, most likely because it divides by the number of things a shopper bought this month, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No staged rollout of the flag change was seen. Within the minute it was switched on, most evaluations of monthly-spend-feature returned on, and every evaluation after that minute did.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Had the flag been turned on for a small share of traffic first, with an automatic halt when errors rose, far fewer shoppers would have hit the failing page before it was stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that exercises the flag-gated monthly summary with the flag on, for a shopper with past purchases but none this month, before the flag could be enabled in production.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division error would have been caught before the flag reached shoppers, and the incident would not have happened.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator Agent formed the candidate that turned out to be the cause, C1, {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus read the flag provider's history beyond the window the investigation's change reads covered. That surfaced the later an-unrelated-feature change so it could be weighed and ruled out.
The Mitigation Agent turned monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and the metrics show the service back to normal from that instant.
Argus confirmed, {T21.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, that turning the flag off had brought the service back.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #403 {T23.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this alert, so no person was brought in when it fired.

input.root_cause: The monthly spend summary, which `render_spend_summary` runs only when `use_monthly_summary` is on, computes the average spend per item this month by integer-dividing the month's total by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty division is still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers who have bought before but nothing this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
